prompt: US home solar installations grew 30% a year for five years. This year they fell 10%, after the largest state ended its installation subsidy. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Installations grew 30% a year, then fell 10% after the largest state's subsidy ended.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: It could be the subsidy, interest rates, panel prices, installer capacity or demand saturation.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: The subsidy ending caused the decline, so the industry will keep shrinking.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: The end of the subsidy in the largest state likely explains most of the decline.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd compare installation trends in that state with the rest of the country.

explanation: The timing points to the subsidy. Comparing the subsidy state with the others separates its effect from national factors.

distractor_flaws.M.restates_facts: Installations grew 30% a year, then fell 10% after the largest state's subsidy ended.
distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be the subsidy, interest rates, panel prices, installer capacity or demand saturation.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: The subsidy ending caused the decline, so the industry will keep shrinking.
